text:
maria: Heads up — seeing ~30% of new GPU nodes in eu-west fail onboarding after yesterday's VPC egress audit-sampler rollout. Logs show repeated NATGW conntrack exhaustion and a few rejected TLS handshakes.

jordan: Ack, noticed node join timeouts too. Are these stuck in provisioning or failing kubelet TLS?

maria: Mostly failing before kubelet registers. TCP resets to our audit shipper IP range, then node never hits our keystore fetch. excerpt from node-agent: `ERROR: dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: connection reset by peer`

alex: That's the new audit-sampler config that adds synchronous forwarding for a subset of flows, right? Could be sending bursts to shipper which overload NAT.

liu: If NAT conntrack is the bottleneck, we can either increase conntrack table or reduce outbound burst. Increasing conntrack has memory/cost tradeoffs.

maria: For immediate mitigation I propose: 1) rollback audit-sampler to async mode in eu-west 2) open ephemeral firewall exception so node onboarding can fetch keystore 3) scale NATGW+conntrack where feasible. Thoughts?

jordan: +1 to rollback first. Can infra-bot run the rollback patch? @infra-bot any ETA? :pray:

infra-bot: Received action: rollback `audit-sampler` in eu-west. Starting rollout to canary hosts (10%); will report status in 5m.

alex: Also curious on long term: audit-sampler sync mode was for stronger sampling guarantees. Maybe we need a buffered proxy in VPC to smooth bursts instead of sync. That would avoid NATGW scaling in every region.

liu: Agreed on buffered proxy. But for compliance we might need sampled delivery ordering guarantees. Could we batch and ack asynchronously with acks to a local agent? Design doc required.

maria: Rollback canary succeeded, infra-bot shows onboard rate normalized on canaries. Rolling full rollback now.

infra-bot: Rollback complete across eu-west by 1718801370. Healthcheck: node-onboard success rate improved from 68% -> 98% in last 10m.

jordan: Nice. Can we capture a timeline + cost impact (natgw bursts) for postmortem? Estimate increased NAT egress and conntrack spikes.

maria: I'll collect metrics: conntrack counts, NATGW pps, #failed-keystore requests, and host-level mem for conntrack. Also will snapshot audit shipper ingestion spikes.

alex: For mitigation plan entry: implement buffered proxy in eu-west AZs, add circuit-breaker on synchronous forwarding, and update rollout gating to include conntrack metrics.

liu: Will start a short RFC for buffered design and include compliance owners. Also note we should add e2e canary test that simulates onboarding under audit bursts.

maria: Filed followups: - postmortem doc link: https://redwood.internal/ops/postmortems/1718801234-audit-sampler-egress - followup RFC PR draft at https://git.internal/rfcs/666

jordan: Thanks, team. Leaving this thread open for any late signals, but rolling back looks good for now. :thumbsup:

alex: FYI I pushed a temporary CloudWatch alarm on conntrack > 180k to catch spikes during rollouts.

maria: Great — closing after we confirm 1h stable.

infra-bot: Monitoring continuing. If node-onboard rate drops below 95% will reopen incident thread.
